check: end-of-run drain path (the stage that killed the previous 24h attempt)
priorFailure: build/s5-stress-before-fix/stress-report.json records passed=false with 'CancellationException: stress stop timed out waiting for in-flight chunks' at the fixed 30s stop timeout.

isTheWindowEnough.note: The window accommodates forty chunks each as slow as the slowest observed, so a timeout would indicate a genuinely stuck future rather than a busy machine.

noServerThreadBlocking.stopReturns: a CompletionStage; the whenCompleteAsync continuation runs on the io executor
noServerThreadBlocking.tickPolling: tick() checks draining.isDone(), a non-blocking test, and returns false while the drain is still running
noServerThreadBlocking.commentInCode: A drain already in progress owns the end of the run; keep ticking so its completions can be delivered, and only finish once it actually settles.
noServerThreadBlocking.whyItMatters: An earlier revision called stop().get() with a 120s budget, turning the end of every run into a single 120s tick and letting the watchdog kill the server at 60s. The current form cannot do that.

failureStaysVisible: If the drain does time out, the CancellationException reaches the report as failure and passed=false, and Test-S5Stress.ps1 now reads that report rather than the exit code - which StressFixture's halt(false) would have left at 0.
